tasks.title: Add Tauri updater plugin configuration
tasks.description: Configure Tauri updater plugin in desktop app with signing keys, update endpoint, and dialog disabled for custom UI.
tasks.details:
1. Add dependency to `desktop/Cargo.toml`:
```toml
[dependencies]
tauri-plugin-updater = "2"
```

2. Register plugin in `desktop/src/lib.rs`:
```rust
use tauri_plugin_updater::Builder as UpdaterBuilder;

#[cfg_attr(mobile, tauri::mobile_entry_point)]
pub fn run() {
    tauri::Builder::default()
        .plugin(tauri_plugin_updater::Builder::new().build())
        // ... other plugins
        .run(tauri::generate_context!())
        .expect("error while running tauri application");
}
```

3. Generate signing keypair using Tauri CLI:
```bash
npm run tauri signer generate -- -w ~/.tauri/animo-updater.key
```

4. Add updater configuration to `desktop/tauri.conf.json`:
```json
{
  "plugins": {
    "updater": {
      "active": true,
      "dialog": false,
      "endpoints": [
        "https://getanimo.app/updates/latest.json"
      ],
      "pubkey": "<PUBLIC_KEY_FROM_GENERATION>"
    }
  }
}
```

5. Backup private key:
- Store in password manager (1Password, Bitwarden, etc.)
- Store in encrypted offline backup (USB drive in safe)
- Test restore from both backups
- Add to GitHub Actions secrets as `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` and `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD`

6. Document key management in internal docs.

IMPORTANT: Never commit the private key to version control. Add `*.key` to `.gitignore`.
tasks.testStrategy: Manual test: Verify plugin builds without errors. Test keypair generation and backup restore. Verify public key is correctly added to tauri.conf.json. Test that GitHub Actions secrets are accessible in workflow. Security review: Verify private key is not in git history or accessible in logs.

tasks.title: Extend release workflow for signed artifacts and manifest publication
tasks.description: Update GitHub Actions release workflow to sign Tauri bundles, upload signatures, and publish the update manifest to the website.
tasks.details:
Modify `.github/workflows/release.yml`:

1. Add secrets to GitHub Actions environment:
- `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY`
- `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD`
- `NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN` (for manifest publication)
- `NETLIFY_SITE_ID`

2. Update each platform build job to sign artifacts:
```yaml
- name: Build and sign Tauri app
  env:
    TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
    TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
  run: npm run tauri build

- name: Upload release assets with signatures
  uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v1
  with:
    files: |
      desktop/target/release/bundle/**/*.dmg
      desktop/target/release/bundle/**/*.dmg.sig
      desktop/target/release/bundle/**/*.AppImage
      desktop/target/release/bundle/**/*.AppImage.sig
      desktop/target/release/bundle/**/*.msi
      desktop/target/release/bundle/**/*.msi.sig
```

3. Add artifact existence checks for .sig files:
```yaml
- name: Check if artifacts exist
  id: check-artifacts
  run: |
    if gh release view ${{ github.ref_name }} --json assets -q '.assets[].name' | grep -q '.sig$'; then
      echo "signatures_exist=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
    fi
```

4. Add manifest publication job that runs after all platform jobs:
```yaml
publish-manifest:
  needs: [build-macos, build-linux, build-windows]
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    
    - name: Download release assets
      run: |
        gh release view ${{ github.ref_name }} --json assets -q '.assets[] | "\(.name) \(.url)"' > assets.txt
    
    - name: Generate update manifest
      run: |
        node scripts/generate-manifest-from-release.js \
          --version ${{ github.ref_name }} \
          --assets assets.txt \
          --output website/public/updates/latest.json
    
    - name: Publish manifest to Netlify
      run: |
        npm install -g netlify-cli
        netlify deploy \
          --dir=website/public/updates \
          --prod \
          --site=${{ secrets.NETLIFY_SITE_ID }} \
          --auth=${{ secrets.NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
```

5. Create `scripts/generate-manifest-from-release.js` to parse GitHub release assets and generate the manifest with correct URLs and signatures.

6. Add validation step to ensure manifest is valid JSON and contains all expected platforms.

tasks.title: Add privacy documentation and update README
tasks.description: Create privacy documentation explaining feedback data handling and update README to direct users to in-app feedback.
tasks.details:
1. Create `docs/privacy.md`:
```markdown
# Privacy Policy

## Feedback Submissions

Animo's in-app feedback feature allows you to send bug reports, feature requests, and questions directly to the development team.

### What We Collect

When you submit feedback through the app, we collect:

- **Required**: Feedback category, title, and description
- **Optional**: Your contact email address
- **Optional**: Diagnostics information (only when you explicitly opt in)

### Diagnostics Information

When you enable the diagnostics checkbox, we collect:

- App version
- Operating system and version
- Platform architecture (e.g., darwin-aarch64)
- System locale
- Recent application log tail (last 50 lines or 2KB)

You can review the exact diagnostics payload before submitting.

### How We Use Your Data

- Feedback submissions create GitHub issues in our public repository
- We use this information solely to improve Animo
- We do not sell or share your data with third parties
- We do not collect automatic telemetry or analytics

### Data Storage

- Feedback is stored as GitHub issues
- Unsent drafts are stored locally in your browser's localStorage
- We use Cloudflare Turnstile for spam prevention

### Your Rights

You can:

- Disable feedback submissions in Settings
- Request deletion of your feedback by contacting us
- Submit feedback anonymously (without providing an email)

### Contact

For privacy concerns or data deletion requests, please email: [privacy@getanimo.app]

Last updated: [DATE]
```

2. Update `README.md`:
```markdown
## Feedback and Support

We'd love to hear from you!

### In-App Feedback (Recommended)

The easiest way to send feedback is through the app:

1. Open Settings
2. Go to "Help & feedback"
3. Click "Send feedback"

You can report bugs, request features, or ask questions directly from the app.

### GitHub Issues

You can also [open an issue](https://github.com/captaaint/animo/issues) on GitHub.

### Privacy

See our [Privacy Policy](docs/privacy.md) for details on how we handle feedback data.
```

3. Update `CHANGELOG.md`:
```markdown
## [Unreleased]

### Added
- In-app feedback submission with bug reports, feature requests, and questions
- Diagnostics opt-in for feedback with preview before submission
- Feedback draft persistence in localStorage
- Privacy documentation for feedback data handling
- Tauri auto-updater support with signed release artifacts
- Update banner with download progress and restart action
- Settings controls for update checks and auto-update toggle
- Manual "Check for updates" action in Settings

### Changed
- README now directs users to in-app feedback
- Settings now includes "Help & feedback" section
```

4. Add configuration to `app/src/config.ts`:
```typescript
export const FEEDBACK_ENDPOINT = 
  import.meta.env.VITE_FEEDBACK_ENDPOINT || 
  'https://getanimo.app/api/feedback';

export const UPDATE_MANIFEST_URL = 
  import.meta.env.VITE_ANIMO_UPDATES_URL || 
  'https://getanimo.app/updates/latest.json';

export const TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY = 
  import.meta.env.VITE_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY || 
  '<PRODUCTION_SITE_KEY>';
```
